power.rule: you share a dream world with whoever is sleeping physically closest to you
power.look: cyan dream glow, proximity HUD rings, nightmare red distortion

script.text: You're dreaming you can fly. Suddenly, your little sister drops from the sky riding a giant goldfish.
Because her bedroom is three meters away.
Next night, Mo sleeps on your floor. Your dream becomes a laser battle with infinite pizza.
Third night, you walk into your secret dream vault. And your sister is standing there reading your diary.
What if dreams were multiplayer? The rule: you share a dream with whoever is sleeping physically closest to you.
At first, it's the ultimate co-op game. Sleepovers become superhero movies. You build entire worlds before breakfast.
Until you take an overnight red-eye flight.
In REM sleep, your amygdala fires thirty percent hotter than when awake, while your brainstem paralyzes your muscles. That's real.

Inside a cabin six meters wide, two hundred passengers enter REM sleep together. One person has a nightmare. And the terror infects the entire plane. Two hundred strangers trapped in one monster, unable to scream, unable to wake up.
When you land, men in dark suits seal the gate. They know what happened.
And tonight, your little sister just fell asleep next door with a fever.
And the walls are starting to melt. Part one.

science.claim: In REM sleep, your amygdala fires thirty percent hotter than when awake.
science.working: Neuroimaging studies (PET and fMRI) measuring cerebral blood flow and glucose metabolism show the limbic system, particularly the amygdala, increases activity by 20% to 33% during REM sleep compared to waking rest (Braun et al., 1997; Maquet et al., 1996), driving hyper-intense emotional dreams.
science.source: Maquet et al., 'Functional neuroanatomy of human rapid-eye-movement sleep and dreaming', Nature 1996; Braun et al., 'Regional cerebral blood flow throughout the sleep-wake cycle', Brain 1997

science.claim: Your brainstem paralyzes your muscles in REM sleep.
science.working: During REM sleep, REM atonia prevents enacting dreams via glycinergic and GABAergic motor neuron inhibition originating in the sublaterodorsal nucleus (SLD) and ventromedial medulla.
science.source: Luppi et al., 'The neuronal network of REM sleep sleep-paralysis', Sleep Med Rev 2011

science.claim: Cabin six meters wide, two hundred passengers in REM sleep.
science.working: Standard commercial wide-body airliners (e.g. Boeing 787 / Airbus A330) have cabin interior widths of 5.5 to 5.6 meters and seat 200 to 300 passengers within a dense cylinder, placing all passengers within a 3-meter physical radius of neighbors.
science.source: Boeing 787 Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning; Airbus A330 Aircraft Characteristics
